records.purpose: Copy the current storage session generation, ordinary own table count and open cursor count into a size-prefixed record.
records.buffer_contract:
`sco_result (*owner_info)(sco_plugin* self, sco_storage_owner_info* out);`
Copy the current storage session generation, ordinary own table count and open cursor count into a size-prefixed record.
records.ownership: Caller-owned copied metadata only; self selects its existing database. No paths, stored values, raw handles or other-owner selector. Output records require full declared size; trailing bytes preserved.
records.thread_affinity: Any thread; serialize per owner with ordinary storage operations. SQL progress budget applies; mutex scheduling has no hard deadline.
records.callback_context: No caller/provider callbacks; views and virtual tables are not executed.
records.reentrancy: Recursive same-call use unspecified; no callback entrypoint is supplied.
records.results: Absent service: NOT_FOUND; incompatible version: UNAVAILABLE. Unopened/stopped storage: UNAVAILABLE; invalid/released self or malformed/short records: BAD_ARG. Missing/excluded table: NOT_FOUND. Allocation: TOO_MANY; SQL failure/interruption: FAILED. Failure leaves outputs untouched except next_table short-name TOO_MANY writes required size only.
records.absent_capability: The separate metadata service is NOT_FOUND on an old host; a short/null member must be treated as UNAVAILABLE, not successful zero.
records.cleanup: No metadata resource or cursor ownership escapes. Ordinary storage owner release/Stop invalidates access; storage generations distinguish successful restarts. Retained faults do not authorize cleanup.
limitations: Interval observations, not a transaction across concurrent writes.
Metadata never opens a database; expensive counts may fail within the SQL budget.
The experimental Rust binding has no typed metadata wrapper.
